title: tier-2 shipped code: the single-property record query at 0x140cb3990

unreachableBranches.why: the null-record test only fires when the array pointer is null with a nonzero count; the window read of the same record faults before it, so the edge cannot execute

notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is `crates/ow-sim/src/modifiers.rs` (`apply_property_records`), called through the `mover_property_records` entry.

`FUN_140cb3990` walks the 0x38-byte records at `body+0x870` (count `+0x878`), keeps those whose window `[+0x1c,+0x20)` holds the frame id `body+0xe4`, and applies the op at `+0x2c` for every record whose `+0x28` equals the caller's property. It is the function the jump stage calls for properties 0x14, 0x15 and 0x26.

The oracle reads the records from the arena address in `body+0x870`; the candidate receives the same bytes as its fourth argument because the probe has no address space. The value is a `float*` on both sides, so the mutated float is the second channel; the returned byte is the client's `bl` (`0x140cb3a8a`), set by any record matching the window and the property, even with an out-of-range op.

Cases cross the six in-range ops and two out-of-range ones with a NaN, both infinities, signed zero and the equal-operand cases, plus window edges, a property mismatch and several matching records in table order.
The six-entry op jump table at `0x140cb3af8` is read as image data; it is declared in `allowedImageReads` because the oracle has to read it to dispatch.
acknowledgedGaps: The record producer is not covered here: the fixture builds the array itself, so this unit proves the applier, not where the records come from (open, `docs/open-questions.md`).
